questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

I can't ________ this heat anymore.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'bear'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence** 'bear'** should be used in the blank.
 
• **"Can't" **is the contraction of **"cannot,"** indicating ***an inability or lack of capability to do something.***
 
• **"Bear" **here means to endure or tolerate. In this sentence, it expresses the inability to continue enduring or tolerating the heat.
 
• So, when someone says* "I can't bear this heat anymore," *it means they have reached a point where they are finding it very difficult or impossible to tolerate or endure the high temperature any longer. They're expressing their discomfort and inability to handle the heat. 

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *I can't **bear** this heat anymore.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.**

I __need to put out__ my clothes before I leave for work this morning otherwise, I will be restless when I return.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'need to put away'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is** grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, **'need to put away'** should be used instead of** 'need to put out'.**
 
• **"Put out" **typically means *to extinguish something or to place something outside*, while **"put away" **means *to store or place something in its proper location.*
 
• Here's why **"put away"** is more fitting in this context:
 
 
• *"I need to put away my clothes before I leave for work this morning otherwise, I will be restless when I return."*
 
• This implies that the clothes will be properly** stored or placed in their designated locations**, like in a closet or dresser. When using *"put away,"* it indicates a sense of organization and tidiness, ensuring that the clothes are stored properly and not left out.
 
 
 
• So, if the intention is to ensure the clothes are neatly stored or arranged in their proper place before leaving for work to avoid feeling restless upon return,** "put away"** would be more suitable than **"put out."** 

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *I **need to put away** my clothes before I leave for work this morning otherwise, I will be restless when I return.*

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.**

With reference of your letter, the organisation wishes to hire you for the security services.

options.text: the organisation wishes to hire you

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'With reference of your letter'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'With reference to your letter'** should be used instead of **'With reference of your letter'.**
 
• The preposition **"of"** is not typically used in English after **"reference"** in this context. Instead, the more commonly accepted and grammatically appropriate phrase would be **"With reference to your letter."**
 
• The corrected version uses **"to"** after **"reference,"** aligning with standard English usage. This construction indicates that the organization is considering or acknowledging the contents or information provided in the letter as the basis for their decision to hire for security services.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***With reference to your letter**, the organisation wishes to hire you for the security services.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The boy will bring the coffee.

options.text: The coffee will be brought by the boy.
The coffee will have been brought by the boy.
The coffee would have been brought by the boy.
The coffee must have been brought by the boy.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The coffee will be brought by the boy.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it to Passive Voice.
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'The boy'. 
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'the coffee'. 
 
• Since **a modal verb **has been used in **the active voice**, therefore,** the passive voice **will follow the given structure:-
 
 
• Active Voice - Subject + modal verb*(will) *+ V1 + Object.
 
• Passive Voice - Object(Subjective form) modal verb*(will)* + be + V3 Subject (Objective form).
 
 
 
• Here, 'will bring' is changed into 'will be brought' because in the 'active to passive' transformation third form of the verb is used.
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the above-mentioned points, we find that the correct answer is Option 1. 

 ​

Correct Sentence:__ *The coffee will be brought by the boy.*

questions.question:
**Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

A. By conquest, rather than by economic contract

B. Other types of feudalism was the relation

C. The principal difference between Indian and

D. Between lord and vassal, established in this case
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'C, B, D, A'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
 
• The first **sentence** will be **sentence** **C** because this fragment follows the initial part and hints at the main difference present in other forms of feudalism.
 
• After it, **Sentence B** will be used because this fragment follows the initial part and hints at the main difference present in other forms of feudalism. 
 
• **Sentence D** will be the third sentence because this fragment adds specificity by highlighting the particular aspect that distinguishes the relationships in Indian feudalism from other types: the relationship between the lord and vassal.
 
• Finally, **Sentence A** will be used because this fragment concludes the sentence by explaining how this relationship between the lord and vassal was established in the case of Indian feudalism, emphasizing that it was established through conquest, unlike economic contracts seen in other feudal systems.

 
 
 

**Correct Order:__** *The principal difference between Indian and other types of feudalism was the relation between lord and vassal, established in this case by conquest, rather than by economic contract.*

questions.question:

The correct answer is** 'United we stand, divided we fall'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate idiom for the given statement would be** "united we stand, divided we fall."**
 
• This **idiom** highlights **the importance of unity in facing challenges or dangers**. It means that when people come together and stay united, they are stronger and more likely to overcome difficulties. Conversely, if people are divided or separated, they are weaker and more likely to fail.
 
• So, in the context of the statement, **it emphasizes the necessity of unity to effectively combat any danger.​**

**Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Under a cloud: This idiom is used to describe a situation or person that is under suspicion or in disfavor. For example, if someone is suspected of doing something wrong, they can be said to be "under a cloud."
 
• Up a blind alley: This phrase signifies a course of action that leads nowhere or has no prospects of positive outcome. It's like following a path that leads to a dead-end, symbolizing wasted efforts or a situation with no positive solution in sight.
 
• Well begun is half done: This saying means that a good start to a task or project makes it easier to complete. It emphasizes the importance of starting work with strong preparation or effort, suggesting that a task is halfway to completion if its beginning is handled well.
